subject: Combiner bake-off status
body:
Hi both,

Benchmark status: at 8k context the axial variant matches our full-attention baseline's perplexity within 0.3% at roughly 40% of the attention FLOPs; mixture closes the gap entirely but gives back a third of the savings. The fixed-pattern variant falls off at longer contexts, as expected. logn looks best asymptotically but, per Ivo's earlier flag, it's JAX-only.

At 32k (the product target) axial holds: 1.1% perplexity gap, attention cost scaling near sqrt as advertised.

Trade-off for the 5/8 decision: axial (cheapest, tiny quality gap, exists in both frameworks) vs mixture (no quality gap, less savings). My lean is axial — the 0.3-1.1% gap is below what our downstream evals can detect.

Risk: Nikhil found nondeterminism in the TF eval path; being chased this week, doesn't affect the JAX numbers.

Yusuf
